utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic. Cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Kapetanovic. As you probably remember, yesterday we commenced our cross-examination, and we left it off with the sketches. And we agreed that it was possible that there were actually eight entrances into your apartment building, but as far as I'm concerned, we can close that topic. I would like to check something else with you. You spoke about where the apartment of Simo Zaric was located, and this can be found in transcript on page 8887, line 20 and 21. And I remember you saying that the apartment was on the third floor, which means that if we count the ground floor as the first floor, that means that his apartment was actually on the fourth floor. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If Mr. Simic and I lived on the same floor, it's what we call third floor, including the ground floor. So the ground floor, first floor, second, third floor. This is how we counted, as living on the third floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam Kapetanovic, let's clarify just one thing. If I heard you correctly, you mentioned Mr. Simic, and I am talking about Mr. Zaric. So let's just make sure that we have no misunderstanding there. We are talking about Mr. Zaric. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are talking about my neighbour Mr. Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So I checked the transcript again, page 8887, and in line 20 and 21 - I'm saying this for my friends - it says as follows: [In English] [Previous translation continues] "... entrance. I don't know the apartment number, but if we take into consideration that we begin with ground floor, he was on the third floor, but it was the fourth landing." Then after that there was a question: "So I understand, then, that he was -- his apartment would have been one level higher than yours. Is that correct?" That was the question of the Prosecution. And you answered: "I believe it is correct." And you -- "I must also add that I never visited Mr. Zaric." [Interpretation] So you see, Mrs. Kapetanovic, the transcript is fairly clear regarding this, so we should call this third floor and fourth level. And this is exactly what the Prosecutor asked you, whether his apartment was one level above yours, and you confirmed that to the Prosecutor. So are you adhering to your previous statement or would you like to make some corrections?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that in my previous testimony I used the word "I think" or "I believe," and I'm perfectly clear on this today, if I go back ten years, when I lived in that apartment, I can tell you that I remember all of the entrances very well, albeit I don't like to remember them, and I can correct my previous hesitation when I said "I think," "I believe" and confirm that now it was on the same level as my apartment, level 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, so if I understood you correctly, you remain by what you stated here previously, third floor, fourth level.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am repeating here that it was third floor, the same level as my apartment. We had the ground floor in our entrance, and there was a young man named Hasan who lived on the ground floor. On the first floor there was a woman called Mina living, and above her was a very large apartment of Mr. Simo Zaric. Count it any way you want, but this is what the order of the apartment was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. So according to what you just told us, Mr. Simo Zaric's apartment was on the second floor; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Second floor, third level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, madam. Since transcript was not entirely clear, I think we clarified it perfectly now. This entrance that you mentioned in the apartment building number 62, was it entrance -- the entrance with the greatest number of apartments? Because there were apartments on both sides of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That segment of the building has five entrances. I don't know how I came to forget the entrance in which my very good friend lived, Mr. Halilovic Dedo. You know that for a while I took shelter in the basement of his mother-in-law. So that part of the building has the greatest number of entrances, and my part of the building has three entrances. If I had a sketch here, I could show it all to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, I think that we clarified this enough. I talked about it to Mr. Zaric, using the record in the transcript, based on your testimony, and there were some things that were not correct, but I believe that we clarified all of that now, including this entrance number 8 in which Dedo Halilovic's apartment was and the entrance in which the apartment of Mr. Zaric was. So that is all clear now. Mrs. Kapetanovic, when we listened to you giving testimony here, we heard you describe the episode in which you saw the accused here, Mr. Simic and Mr. Zaric, and you said that you did not see them enter the apartment of Mr. Zaric; you just saw them in the entrance and assumed that they were going to visit Mr. Zaric in his apartment. I suppose that you concluded this based on the fact that there were members of the same party and the same unit, and this can be found on transcript page 8887, lines 2 and 3. And then later on, when asked by the Prosecutor, you stated this again, on page 8889 of the transcript, lines 19 and 21. So if I understood you correctly, you saw -- or you concluded that Mr. Simic and Mr. Tadic went to visit Mr. Zaric in his apartment, and you concluded this based on the fact that they belonged to the same party and to the same unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. You are asking me whether I made a conclusion of that sort. Now, would you make a conclusion along the following lines: My husband used to play an instrument, and if there were other musicians entering the apartment, would you conclude that they went to see my husband as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I will do my best to control the witness and to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness, Mrs. Kapetanovic, you are here to answer questions from counsel, and do not ask counsel any questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right, madam. Well, my question was along the following lines: Did you make that conclusion based on the fact that they belonged to the same party and to the same unit?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, with respect to that fact, we have a number of contradictory information, both the ones existing in this Tribunal and the ones that emerged from the testimony of other witnesses. Let's take the first point first. Were they members of the same party? Based on what you said, I conclude that you believe that Mr. Zaric was a member of the SDS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on what happened later on, I concluded that their ideas were the same, and what the political party of each of them was called, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, all I wanted to ask you, whether you concluded that Mr. Simo Zaric was a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question regarding the unit. I believe that you had in mind the 4th Detachment. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, based on your answer, I conclude that you believed Mr. Blagoje Simic to be a member of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blagoje Simic at that time was the most important man in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, all I'm interested in is the 4th Detachment. Did you conclude that Blagoje Simic was the member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I supposed he was. I assumed he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, now we are obviously referring to the time before April 17th, so you assumed that Blagoje Simic was a member of the 4th Detachment? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I talked to my client regarding these facts, and I received the following information from him: First, he claims that he has never been a member of the SDS but rather of the SDP. Second, he claims that Blagoje Simic was never a member of the 4th Detachment, that the physician of the 4th Detachment was Mr. Sisic. And third, he claims that Blagoje Simic never entered his apartment, nor did Miroslav Tadic. My client says that he met with Mr. Tadic frequently, that they saw each other at the Cafe AS, but his apartment was never entered, either by Mr. Simic or by Mr. Tadic. So can you continue to claim what you have claimed before?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I never saw anybody entering the apartment of Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Another question that has to do with it as well. Do you know that Mr. Blagoje Simic also lived in this apartment building number 62?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But you don't know that he actually resided in that apartment building. He moved there somewhere in 1990, 1991.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I never entered the entrance 7, I only went to entrance 8, I don't know the residents of that -- or tenants of that entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It looks that I was not -- one part of my question was not interpreted. I said entrance number 7. It was building number 62, and then entrance number 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. All right. So you've completed it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But I believe that I don't need further clarification from the witness, because she already answered that she was not familiar with that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I have just a few more questions. Your then boyfriend and current husband, Esref, can you confirm that before the war, before April 17th, Mr. Simo Zaric was a friend of his father and his grandfather, that they were on very friendly, close terms?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And very briefly: You already described to us the incident in which your then boyfriend and current husband came to see you and that he then asked Mr. Zaric to help you, to which Mr. Zaric replied that he was unable to help. Can you confirm that Mr. Zaric at that time told to your boyfriend that he was not authorised to do anything with respect to that? Can you remember that or not? If you cannot, just please say so.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My husband went to see him and asked for help. That is true. I remember that he said that Simo was not in the situation to be able to help. I don't remember him mentioning anything about being authorised, but all of us know what kind of authorities Mr. Zaric had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I asked you yesterday about this, and this will be my last question. Yesterday we mentioned the 4th Detachment quite a bit. We also mentioned the pheasant farm, and you, during your testimony, mentioned many other things. I just wanted to clarify one more matter. Perhaps this is not very important to you whether somebody is a member of the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, or 5th Detachment, but it's a very important matter here before this Trial Chamber. Can you tell me, please: At the pheasant farm, and in other places where there were checkpoints of the 4th Detachment, how did you know that those were members of the 4th Detachment manning those checkpoints and not members of the 2nd, 3rd, or 5th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were people from the vicinity of Samac, from its environs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that that's enough in terms of an answer, because to you it was probably very important whether the people were from Samac or from its surrounding areas. So at those checkpoints, the people that were manning them were actually from the surrounding areas?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At the checkpoint in Zasavica camp, at the entrance, there was Nenad Lukic, his cousin Lukic, and other gentlemen from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Madam, we are confusing some things. I didn't ask you specifically about the checkpoint at Zasavica. I asked you about the road to Odzak. There were checkpoints there, and you asked [As interpreted] that some were manned by the men from Krajina and some by the members of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You reminded me about it. The man who was manning the checkpoint at Odzak was a policeman from Bosanski Samac, Mirko, and I cannot remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was it Mirko Pavic, by any chance?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to apologise. I cannot recall his last name at this very moment, but I will recall it a bit later on. It was a policeman from Bosanski Samac. It is possible that his last name was Pavic, although I can't claim it with certainty. But he was a policeman from Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, madam. We are not challenging that. We are not challenging any of that. I'm just referring to the checkpoints. I'm not really interested in who manned them. You spoke about the fact that there was the zone of responsibility for the 4th Detachment, so I'm not interested in specific people who were there but somebody was in charge in Odzak and somebody was in charge elsewhere, but you believe that people in charge there were not from Samac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Savo Cancarevic was in charge of the checkpoint near the camp in Crkvina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've been trying to follow this, and I don't want to interrupt, but now I'm -- I'm very confused. We have at least on the English transcript a lot of talking about checkpoints there, checkpoints here, who was manning them, then I'm not really interested in who manned them, and I can't follow now which checkpoint we're talking about. "You believe people in charge there were not from Samac." Again, I just ask Mr. Lazarevic to be more clear on which checkpoints he's talking about because when the witness answers, "Well in Odzak they were there," and he says, "Oh, I'm not talking about that. I'm talking about something else." And finally I have to the stage where I really have no idea any longer which checkpoints where we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So at least one -- the answer for the checkpoint near the camp in Crkvina is clear. The witness has said it was Savo Cancarevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That and the one at Odzak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we make clear the one at Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Or whichever one Mr. Lazarevic is asking. I think the witness has always been very clear in her answer about which checkpoint she is talking about. I'm more concerned about which checkpoints Mr. Lazarevic is asking about. He hasn't, to the best of my knowledge, not specified any location any time he's put a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Lazarevic, you heard the Prosecution's --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I have just read what my learned colleague from the Prosecution said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you clear that part of the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was the checkpoint at the pheasant area that this witness was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, madam. Well, let's try to elicit yes or no answers from you and I will try to put my questions accordingly. Madam, the pheasant farm, was it located on the territory of Odzak municipality?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the checkpoint near the pheasant farm, was it the man from Krajina, members of that army, who controlled that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just that checkpoint out of all of the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more question. The entire time we covered here, you know which period we had in mind, we in fact referred to the Army of Republika Srpska; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "the entire time"?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, madam, I have in mind the time period when you went to do forced labour.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time it was the army, but I don't know whose army it was. Everybody thought themselves to be very important and more important than the others, so I didn't really pay much attention to whom did they actually belong.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The next counsel, if any. Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Kapetanovic. My name is Dragan Krgovic, and on behalf of the Defence team of Mr. Miroslav Tadic, I will be putting some questions to you. Just like my colleague Lazarevic, I will try to formulate my questions in such a way as to allow you to give me a yes or no reply. If you cannot answer a question, just please say so, or if you do not remember some details, again feel free to tell us, and if any explanations are needed, then that can be covered in the re-direct with the Prosecution. Mrs. Kapetanovic, on the 4th of June, you answered questions put to you by the Prosecution, and at that time you mentioned that you frequently passed by the Cafe AS when going from your apartment to the downtown area. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned the fact that the wife of Mr. Miroslav Tadic was the owner of the shop that you frequented and that that shop was by the Cafe AS. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The shop was sometime before the developments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was it in March or April 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at that time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So as I understood you, because in the transcript of the 4th of June, 2002, from that answer, we could infer that the shop worked at the time, and next to the shop, that Mr. Tadic kept -- had the Cafe AS. So let us clear that up. So the shop in April -- March/April 1992 didn't exist?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I believe it was a gambling casino.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Are you speaking of Cafe AS or the premises next to Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I said that I never entered into the Cafe AS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you knew that there was a casino there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never been in the casino, but I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the shop. Was it in the Cafe AS before the premises were transformed in the cafe, or was the Cafe AS next to the shop?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I stated that I, prior to the war, didn't like to pass by Cafe AS. Namely, I didn't even enter these premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you liked to go to the shop?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period when the situation was normal. I don't think that I stated which period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll go back to what you stated on the 4th of June. That was page 8891?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we just clarify this instead of going back and forth? I'll ask the witness. When -- which period did you frequent this shop next to Cafe AS? Was it before March/April 1992 or any other time? Because you're saying that -- it seems to me there was a specified period, before March and April 1992. Can you just clarify that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It refers to the period prior to 1992. I'm speaking of the time of normality, of a normal life in our town. I'm speaking of the period when groups were appearing of aliens, people who were not from Samac, and the period when I didn't like passing by. And so that I don't have an insight into what Mr. Tadic possessed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So is it clear, then, or are you saying that you used to frequent this shop before the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. That was precisely what I wanted to ask, because in the question of the Prosecution, when the Prosecution asked whether she liked and was passing by at that period, the answer was that she liked going to the shop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I preferred going to a shop that was behind the building, by the family of -- the Tadic family. It was a different shop. I was referring to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to ask you something about the guests, the patrons of Cafe AS. Do you remember saying that you knew the patrons were members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And that were also the people sitting in the garden of Cafe AS?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was it usual that people -- that patrons sit in a cafe, they would sit there if they were workers and they would sit in the nearby cafes at the breaks?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be so, but we also had our favourite spots, including myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Kapetanovic, do you know that right across the street from Cafe AS the so-called Sit building, the textile industry building was right across there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: As you were passing by on a daily basis, do you remember that in the period of March, April, and even prior to that, in front of the Sit building, there was a Yugoslav flag was flying on the building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many of us tried at the time to be good Yugoslavs, and possibly there was this flag flying. And I never had anything against that flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, concerning your personal knowledge, do you know that the 4th Detachment's headquarters were in the Sit building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I can only say what I know, or exclusively that what I had seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And do you know --

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only what I had seen, if that is what interests you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the Sit factory, the headquarters of the 4th Detachment were located?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned that passing by the AS cafe, you observed patrons who were people not from Samac.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear any -- how they talked, whether they were using the Ekavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Ekavian, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: To the Prosecutor, you said that it was in March and April 1992. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the period prior to the war. It could refer to these two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And possibly also earlier?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Earlier, I did not notice, observe such things. We lived more normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking January, February, March, so it would be these -- the first three months of the year.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. January, February, obviously nobody would be sitting outside on the terrace, so I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you observe this beginning or the end of March?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sure they were there in front of -- before the war, immediately, but how long it was, I wouldn't know, and at a certain point it was such an important topic for all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the Cafe AS there was a casino? You said you heard about that. Do you know that people from Yugoslavia and abroad, card players, would come and play here, and the gamblers --

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gamblers were then people who were shelling me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that it was unpleasant for you to pass by the Cafe AS. How long was this period of unpleasantness for you? A month, two months, that people were commenting when you were passing by?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to the period prior to the war, two weeks, 20 days. I didn't count the days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned to the Prosecutor that you saw these people on the terrace in the morning, in the afternoon, and in the evening, throughout the day. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only -- yes. Only the faces would change.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: These were people of middle age, middle-aged people. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This age of mine, what do I say -- what do I mean by saying "middle-aged people"? I believe these were able people, able to fight, fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm 40. Would I belong to the category of middle-aged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're young and you certainly belong in that category.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, we will pass on to another topic, the evening of the 16th, on the 17th of April, 1992. In the night on the 16th, 17th, you stated to the Prosecutor that the information concerning what was happening in Samac, that you received that, the information, from your neighbours. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the entire scene, and this, if I mention this, it's only a part of the entire scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm only asking about how you received the information, about receiving the information, and this is the topic of my questions.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information was -- or the discussion, rather, was who will attack Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You've already stated that to the Prosecutor. You explained that part. I'm only interested in some other aspects you mentioned and some clarifications. Namely, you said you didn't have a telephone in the apartment and that you used Salko Porobic's telephone.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You also stated that you heard that in Samac battles were under way between the 4th Detachment, special units, and people who wished to save the town and who belonged to the SDA. Do you remember -- do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you've placed them all in the same category, and something isn't right in how you ranked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the fighting was going on between the 4th Detachment and the specialised units, on the one hand, and the people who wished to save the town and who belonged to the SDA. And if I correctly interpreted your words. That was on page 8896.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember stating that. In a mildly, moderately put sentence, I might have stated it in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: 8898. I will read this sentence [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... party. [Interpretation] This is what you stated.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the fighters belonged to that party, but that wasn't the priority. The defenders were a handful of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's written there, then I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Salko Porobic was a member --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, you're not waiting for the interpretation to be completed. Please remember that. You can repeat your question, because it wasn't completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Salko Porobic was a member of that unit, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you believe member of that party?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: No. The unit which fought in that battle, in the combat.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never participated in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying in combat for the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salko Porobic was a member of SDA. He never concealed that. And at his age, he was certainly -- he wasn't fit to fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was a member of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't boast about it. I wasn't interested. I didn't ask, nor do I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he convey this information about the combat taking place between the 4th Detachment, the special units, and a group of citizens, inhabitants, members of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This knowledge was imparted to me in the form of a mosaic from the tenants living in my building of all nationalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What did Salko impart to you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That what he found out by telephone, that there was serious combat, heavy battles, that people have been killed, that the situation is serious, and that there's no way out of Samac. And sir, I believe that that was my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did Salko receive this information from his -- from the members of his party? Did he say anything in that connection?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salko Porobic is an inhabitant with a big family, numerous family in that town, who knows everyone, and everybody knows him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I only asked about the source of information. Please, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, you were in good relations with Salko Porobic and his family?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Salko Porobic told you that he took some rifles from the association of the handicapped, whose member he was.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'd be very grateful to my learned colleague if he could tell me if he is now quoting from a transcript something the witness has claimed to have said in her prior testimony for the Bench, because I don't recall this being part of the record. And counsel seems to have put to her that she claims that Salko had told her --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And I have no recollection of it. And if it is in the record and I just can't remember it, I'd like to be told where so that I can confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to explain. These are questions which are based on Rule 90(H). 90(H), where questions can be -- and I quote -- that the witness can make an important statement for the issue. She also mentioned, although this wasn't in the examination-in-chief, we believe that this can enter into the cross-examination, in view of Rule 90(H).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I understand what you're saying. I think it's the way in which it was put to the witness, because it appeared as if this is what the witness had said. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, did Salko Porobic state to you that he was also in the scout formations of the -- and that he entered them prior to -- immediately prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he hid those rifles with his sister-in-law Behka?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this woman had very great problems in the SUP, when Mr. Simo Zaric was there, and that she was called in for questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether these rifles were found in her place? Answer, please, with a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Salko Porobic hid -- that he hid himself and that he was being looked for in connection with these rifles; at the end he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, I said that Salko Porobic was attending lunch every day at my place, with the other tenants, and I'm surprised that he -- you're saying that he was in hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I'm asking you whether you know certain facts, with a "yes," or "no," or "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salko Porobic did not go into hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He was in his apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't sleep in his apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, but I certainly do not control where men sleep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: How did you know that he didn't go into hiding?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that such an older man, maybe he can be afraid. He was alone and bombs were falling, hitting higher floors, and it's logical that he went to the lower floors, as I did with my family, with my boyfriend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, you said that you received certain information from your neighbour Djordje Tubakovic. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: That was on page 8900 and 8901. There you were describing that you received information how to behave when people come and search your apartment, that you have to leave the door open, that you should stand by the door with your feet spread, legs apart, spread.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me: When did he state this to you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That morning when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In the morning or that evening?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That morning when the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to the arrival of these uniformed persons in your entrance or at the time?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to the arrival of these uniformed and armed persons coming to our entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you took this warning seriously?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After being warned that people had been killed, after such information arrived by telephone, of course I took it seriously. I feared it. And I also tried to create a normal situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: On the 4th of June you were answering the questions of the Prosecutor - that is on page 8901 - that you heard a noise in the hall and that on the basis of that, you concluded that the soldiers entered the hallway. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The noise could be heard not only that it was reverberating in the entire building, but it was reverberating also in one head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But when the soldiers entered, the moment they entered the building, you did not see it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated where I was at the time. I couldn't see downward. But what I did see, I stated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: They were -- the door was unlocked by Djordje Tubakovic. He led them in, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer is that we couldn't even close that door, not to speak of locking that door.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, we received information that a month earlier that door had been repaired and that it was -- it could close and that it could be locked.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very possible. Possibly it's so, but who unlocked and opened the door, to whom, I neither saw nor stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tubakovic's apartment is below your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A floor lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The apartment of Salko Porobic was above your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Incidentally, let me ask you: You mentioned the age of Salko Porobic. Is he about the same age as Mr. Tadic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you that Salko Porobic had two heart attacks, and I was present at that unfortunate event. I never ask men about their age. It's a bit embarrassing for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: At the place where you were standing, were you able to see them as they left the building? You said that they went outside. Were you able to see the level, the floor on which the apartment of Mr. Tubakovic is?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stood between my apartment and Mr. Tubakovic's apartment, so I was able to see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Djordje Tubakovic is a Serb, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please, was it customary in that period of time, in Samac, in the beginning of 1992, for people to take off their shoes when they enter somebody's apartment and leave the shoes by the entrance door?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about that. It is quite typical, especially in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether there were many pairs of shoes in front of the apartment of Djordje Tubakovic, in front of the door to his apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That morning I was in the apartment of Mr. Tubakovic as well and I didn't count how many shoes there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me be more specific, then. Weren't all of your neighbours in his apartment at that time?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were many of us, but I cannot be certain whether there were all of us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Including the family of Porobic, Salko; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about Salko. I know that the entire family went upstairs, downstairs. They were very prone to panic, especially his wife. She would start crying as soon as any dog would bark.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that there were many neighbours at Djordje Tubakovic's apartment, you are referring to the night of 16th and 17th of April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am referring to the time before the very attack on our entrance. By that, I mean that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you were at Djordje Tubakovic's as well that morning; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had coffee at Djordje Tubakovic's that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, when you said that Miroslav Tadic showed up, you said that he was uniformed; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Miroslav Tadic was the only one whose face was not painted over. He was fully armed, he had weapons, pistol, automatic weapons, full military uniform, and all of the rest of the men had their faces painted, so that even God would be unable to recognise them. They looked terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Tadic had an automatic rifle and a pistol?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of those things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And how did he carry these weapons? Was it in his hands or over his shoulder?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The pistol was in his belt and the rifle was on his shoulder, but he kept it in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the soldiers searched all of the apartments in the building looking for weapons. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Everything was searched, but some apartments were searched superficially. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you also stated that Mr. Tadic looked for weapons in the apartment of Salko Porobic.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the apartment of Salko Porobic was searched as well?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very thoroughly searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear or see Mr. Tadic talk to Salko Porobic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the conversations were conducted in the apartment. Some conversations were conducted on the stairwell and some in my apartment. So that means that I was in a situation to follow or to witness most of these conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the conversation between Salko Porobic and Miroslav Tadic. Did you happen to hear that conversation?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you whether the two of them talked privately. I'm not even interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And did they talk to each other in your presence?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their conversation was overheard by the entire building. It was not a normal conversation; it was a very passionate argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you heard that? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Was that conversation taking place in front of the apartment of Djordje Tubakovic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute ago I told you that this conversation took place in many spots. I don't know which parts of this conversation you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we are now talking about the time when Mr. Tadic came to the apartment of Djordje Tubakovic and talked to Mr. Porobic right there.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I gave my statement, I took great care to clearly state where I was at the time, where my then boyfriend, current husband was. These were two priorities that I had in mind at the time when I gave my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, during your testimony, when asked by the Prosecution -- this is something that you touched upon, and all that I'm interested in is this conversation between Mr. Porobic and Mr. Tadic. Did you hear them talk in front of the door of Djordje Tubakovic's apartment? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, the position of my client is significantly different from the one that you are claiming it to be, and it has been brought up many times during these proceedings. Now, first let's check the date. My client states that this event took place on the 18th of April, 1992 and not on the 17th of April. You confirmed this fact because you said that on that day, when the soldiers showed up, all of non-Serb women left the building, and this is something that has been confirmed by other witnesses as well. So are you still standing by that date? Are you still claiming that it was on the 17th of April rather than on the 18th of April? And just to remind you, it was very cold on that day. It started even snowing.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not sure which part of my statement you are challenging. The first person to enter my entrance with a rifle, in the morning, before noon, on the 17th, so the 17th of April, in the morning, before noon, was Miroslav Tadic. He was the first person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So the 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 17th of April. He was the first one who searched my apartment. I don't want you to even bring this into question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, Mr. Miroslav Tadic claims - and this has been confirmed by other witnesses - that he was unarmed on that day. So do you still wish to stand by your previous statement, or rather, let me reformulate this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have, of course, no objection to the Defence counsel putting his client's position about what his client was doing on the 17th of April, but I do object to his statement that "it has been confirmed by other witnesses that he was unarmed on that day," and putting other witnesses as a confirmation of his client's position. He can put his client's position to her and say there's other evidence he was unarmed but to say this is a fact that has been confirmed by other witnesses is not the case, and I don't think he should mix up putting his client's position to the witness and suggesting to the witness that there are confirmed facts before this Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard the objection. I was a bit awkward when formulating my question. This is what I was trying to claim: The position of my client, which can be corroborated by witnesses, is such-and-such. This is what I was trying to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You mean -- when you say which can be corroborated by witnesses, you mean the witnesses he intends to call?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then you can just put it that your instructions from your client are such-and-such, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So madam, the position of my client - and this can be corroborated by eyewitnesses - that he was unarmed on that day. So do you still stand by your previous claim that he was armed on that day? Just briefly, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I swear on God's name, and on everything in the world, that on the 17th of April, the first man to enter our building, fully armed, was Miroslav Tadic. He headed the entire unit. I am not interested in your witnesses, sir. I came here to tell the truth. He came fully armed, Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, let me put another question to you. My client claims that he did not issue orders to anyone that day. So do you still stand by your previous statement that he had issued orders? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: My client claims that on that day he talked to Salko Porobic and Djordje Tubakovic, that Djordje Tubakovic told him that Salko Porobic did not have weapons, he didn't enter the apartment of Salko Porobic, nor was the apartment of Salko Porobic searched on that occasion, or anybody else's apartment, for that matter. So do you still stand by your previous claim that your apartment and other apartments in the building were searched on that day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, apartments were thoroughly searched, my apartment first and then the apartment of Salko Porobic. I will never forget this, and I swear this on God's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you are claiming that the apartment of Salko Porobic was thoroughly searched?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you swear by God that this is God's truth?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Both apartments were thoroughly searched.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Now, to go further on, Mrs. Kapetanovic: My client claims that the military vehicle that you described came only after his leaving the apartment. So do you stand by your previous claim that the vehicle came when he entered the apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came together with that vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't see him arrive?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Miroslav Tadic. You didn't see Mr. Miroslav Tadic as the vehicle drew near. This is what you stated in your statement to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We could see a helmet from above. I couldn't tell whose head was under the helmet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see Mr. Miroslav Tadic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a helmet when he entered the building, since you mentioned this helmet?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was his head gear like, I couldn't tell you, but it wasn't a military cap. I know that for a fact. I know that it was tied under his chin. I don't know what it is called in the military. I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a beard?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen Mr. Miroslav Tadic throughout my life with moustache. I always thought him to be a nice man. I don't think I'll ever change this image that I have of him. I know that he wore a beard for a time, but what he looked like at that very day, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam Kapetanovic, you said that after that event your building and your apartments were searched on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, is it possible that after this event, after this day your apartment was searched many times and you were harassed on many occasions, is it possible that you confused all of these events?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I am not senile. I can confirm everything that is stated in my statement. People who came later on, after this, had nothing to do with Mr. Miroslav Tadic. I had a pistol shoved in my face daily, and I still cannot sleep at night because I think of that. Who was behind this and everything else that happened later, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So it is not plausible that you confused these events?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These events are crystal clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that it was fairly cold at that time, on the 16th and 17th?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was so cold in my heart that I have no idea what the weather was like outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you went fishing on the 16th of April. Was it cold?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the water is always cold.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And the days that preceded the 16th, was it cold on those days?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember what the weather forecast was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm interested in is was the weather typical in March and April for Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The events that followed were so unusual that I simply cannot remember anything usual about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you continued to claim that these people, whom you later described as members of the 4th Detachment, are the people that you continued seeing in March and April sitting on the terrace of Cafe AS.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, these people did sit on the terrace of Cafe AS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What were they dressed like?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I tried not looking at them, let alone observing their clothes. I am not interested in these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to look at their faces? You established that they were non-locals.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I concluded that they were non-locals based on their dialect. They spoke Ekavian. And later on, that became a fashion in our town, so that now I'm not sure who is local and who came from outside. Even I myself am not sure who I belong to any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So you concluded they were non-local based on their dialect?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their accent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And you didn't look at their faces?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look at their faces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: And how come you explained to the Prosecutor later on that you later came to recognise them as members of this unit? Was it only by their dialect?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you clarify the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: You told the Prosecutor that later on, after having contacts with these people, during the activities, exercises of the 4th Detachment, you established that these people belonged to the 4th Detachment. Now you're telling us that you discerned these people based on their accent. So does that mean that later on you recognised them again based on their dialect?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, are you now referring to local people from Samac or to people that came from outside?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: People that came from outside.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the people that came from outside, not locals, can be very easily recognised based on their accent, and you know this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: But madam, you cannot claim that people whom you saw sitting in the Cafe AS were the same people that you later on saw in the uniforms as members of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People who came to my apartment later on were a mix of locals and non-locals, or rather, people with the accent. I firmly claim that I saw both.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you several questions about your contact with Mr. Miroslav Tadic that you described yesterday. You said that the meeting took place after your then boyfriend swam across the Sava River. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that in my statement I said that I applied to Mr. Miroslav Tadic on several occasions. Only once I had an opportunity of being at his place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what I'm referring to now, when you went to visit Mr. Tadic. Did this take place upon your boyfriend's swimming across the river and leaving Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My contact, my only meeting with that man, I think took place before my then boyfriend crossed -- swam across the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Madam, I will put a question to you now which is on page 14. When

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "Mr. Tadic knows that I'm from Croatia. He knows that my entire family belonged to the HVO. He also knew that my boyfriend had escaped and joined the same forces." [Interpretation] Then the Prosecutor went on to ask: [In English] "This meeting took place after the end of August, when your boyfriend had escaped; is that correct?" Answer: Yes. [Interpretation] So you stated to the Prosecutor, fairly clearly and precisely, that your meeting with Miroslav Tadic, in his office, took place after your boyfriend had swum across and left Samac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me remind you --

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: All I'm interested in is whether you stated this here before this Trial Chamber. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's what it says, it is possible that it's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, so did this meeting take place before you were taken to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting took place before I was taken to Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did this meeting take place -- and let me say that the Prosecutor put a second question to you. So you told him that this event took place in the time period between when your boyfriend swam across and you were taken to Zasavica. Is that when this meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat: It is possible that there was a mistake, since there were many attempts made to talk to Mr. Miroslav Tadic.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, this meeting of yours with Mr. Tadic took place in the building that you called the building of local commune. We identified that building before this Trial Chamber as the pensioners' hall. Do you agree with this description? Is it the same building that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on which street you're coming from. If you're coming from the stadium, then it is the hall of pensioners. However, the internal part, inside, are the offices of the local commune. So it is the same building, whatever you call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues].../3. Photo. Can the witness be shown the Exhibit D36/3. Can you put this photograph on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, is it this building that we are referring to?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't know where was this picture taken, but I'm sure that I didn't enter the building from this side. However, I do think it is this building. This photograph is a fairly poor one.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Well, I think we have some better pictures. Let's see what is the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So see, madam, it says here "local commune." Is that what we're talking about, this building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible that it is that building. However, you could place this heading on any building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... /3. 38. D.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you recognise the interior of the building now?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this looks like a typical entrance into any building. I think you would agree with me.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Well, does this interior look familiar to you? That's all I want to ask you. Upon having seen three photographs, can we agree that it's the same building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there was only one building in Bosanski Samac called the pensioners' hall. The pensioners had one part of the building. They had a restaurant there, they played chess there. And the entrance into the local commune building was from a different street, and then passing through the building and going into the courtyard of the same building.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So it is the same building?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it should be the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's time for our break now, and perhaps we can continue after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll take our break and continue at 1100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just ask an indication from Defence counsel how long they will be and if Mr. Pantelic intends to cross-examine just so I can advise when the next witness is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I think I will finish in an hour and a half, to the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- well, I don't know. The questions of my -- and the area which will be covered by my learned friend, let's say half an hour, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The Court will rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. You are continuing with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, we had a break. During our discussion concerning this building. Now I will ask you: You stated in your -- were asked by the Prosecutor that you had to wait prior to entering the Tadic office. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Also, later in your statement, you said that the office of Svetozar Vasovic was next to the office of Mr. Tadic. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I said that it preceded Tadic's office. Maybe I said -- it's been said "next," but it was prior to.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: On the same floor?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him on the same floor.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, it's probably known to you that Miroslav Tadic worked at the time in the civil protection, and are you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that the first combat operations ended, he was -- he acquired a new function; namely, he was the most important man concerning exchanges. Concerning my own interest, he was also responsible for supply. [As interpreted]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: My question concerned his function in the civil protection.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it's called, then that's that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, intervention to the transcript. The witness said, on page 38, line 12, for supply of inhabitants or citizens of Samac. So after the full stop should be -- these words should be added, because that was what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krgovic, you can ask the witness about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam Kapetanovic, you've heard the intervention in the transcript that he was responsible for the supply of the inhabitants, in addition to the other functions.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said what was the truth. I must say, however, that these inhabitants that he was responsible for were of Serb ethnicity, Serb families, and families of those who were at the front lines.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Also burials?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A hundred per cent precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Burials of all inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Burials of the Serb fighters, soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, do you know that Miroslav Tadic and the civil protection organised all burials in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was fortunate that nobody died of my family at the time, but I do know that no Muslim burial could be performed in a similar way as the Serb burials were carried out, and that he didn't allow those ceremonies which pertained to Muslims or Croats.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: My question is: Do you know that he was responsible for that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that each dead person received a coffin, was allotted a coffin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Kapetanovic, just answer the questions which are put to you by counsel. That way we shall move much, much faster.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Could you repeat the question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did you attend Serb burials?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to the war, yes; during the war, no.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And did you attend Muslim burials?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: How did you know that there were differences between the burials of Serbs and Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that quite well.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let me ask another question. Are you aware that Svetozar Vasovic worked in the local Red Cross in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And that in his office of the Red Cross, people applied -- those people applied who wished to go into the exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you know Jovanovic, Anka?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: She also worked in the Red Cross, and before the war in the social work centre?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: She is a Croat?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, married to a Serb.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, I would return to your dialogue with Tadic. In your statement yesterday, in front of this Chamber, you've stated that you offered the apartment and the house for your exchange and that he refused that.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You also testified concerning this dialogue you had with Mr. Tadic, and at the time Mr. Tadic did not say that he knew that your brothers were fighting on the Croatian side.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not say that, but it implied that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Please answer directly. Did he at the time say that he knows that your brothers are fighting in the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did Miroslav Tadic at the time state that your then boyfriend and today husband that he swam over -- crossed over the Sava River, swam over it and joined your brothers? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this point in time, I cannot answer that question. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, I wanted to ask something else. In your statement yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Your Honours. Let me check the transcript, yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, in your testimony, page 13 yesterday, line 25, that your family was in the HVO. But as I understood you, your family lived in Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My family is from Slavonski Samac, and my -- they were members of the HV.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: HVO is -- they were -- they were members of the Croatian army. That is what I wanted to clarify for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And did your boyfriend join them or did he join the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My boyfriend, after crossing towards freedom, went to Bosnia and joined the HVO, another army.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Thank you, ma'am. This is what I wanted to clarify. You also mentioned that he never liked weapons and that Tadic invited him to join the armed forces, that he said he wasn't interested, he doesn't like weapons. Was he mobilised or did he go on a voluntary basis?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He left and fled the mobilisation in Bosanski Samac, and he fled -- and this was the only way that he could get me out of the camp.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: In your testimony, the Prosecutor, you stated that Tadic said that everybody will be able to leave Samac except for you, that you -- it will be very difficult for you.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You stated that in front of this Court.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: But you were exchanged on the 5th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after so many attempts. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Yesterday you stated that after your exchange, you saw some people, men and women, from Zasavica, who were exchanged after you.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the opportunity of meeting people who I got acquainted with during the war.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you know that from your exchange until the end of 1993, over ten exchanges were organised in Samac? Do you know that? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that many exchanges took place, but I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And that you were included in one of the first exchanges?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, how many exchanges took place before yours?
