utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number, but I know that they did take place.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: How many exchanges took place from the time that you signed up, applied for the exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my first application, I believe two or three exchanges took place.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: If we conclude that in 1993 we had ten exchanges, and prior to that, two or three, as you said, you were among the first.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have to tell you: I was very, very sick.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, I'm presenting these facts. I just want to confirm whether you, in view of the number of exchanges and the time, whether you were in one of the first exchanges. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Your injury you've mentioned happened only in the month of September, when you were in Odzak picking plums; wasn't that so?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, I also wanted to ask you: You also testified to the Prosecutor -- you gave a statement to the Prosecutor in May 1998. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You remember that you also had an interview with the Prosecution in May of this year?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the first time that I tried to remember something which I was persistently trying to forget.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: I just asked whether you were interviewed by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you remember that you stated to the Prosecutor -- we received the Prosecutor's note -- you stated that in Zasavica you've heard for the first time that your brother was looking for you and that you were very pleased to hear that. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the first time that I heard that someone from my family was alive.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And then you also heard that your brother was looking for you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you remember when that happened vis-a-vis your arrival to Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told by people when I arrived there.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you remember who told you that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The inhabitants who had a radio receiver.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And of course you wanted to join your family in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logically, that's what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you remember the family Cerninski?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The surname is familiar to me, but I don't recall to whom it applies.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you remember whether any of these -- from these people from this family went with you in the exchange on the 5th of November?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you explain the family?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Cerninski Ferdinand, Cerninski Angela, Cerninski Stipo, Cerninski Aziza.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't born in Samac. I don't know well the families. Now this is a more detailed explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to submit a document as evidence. It is a document which was disclosed to the Prosecution, ERN number Y4786. It is a guarantee for people who wish to go for the exchange and who are travelling to Croatia. In concrete terms, this document is a guarantee for the Cerninski family. We have an official translation of this document, but the seal hasn't been completely translated, but the document itself has been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's dated when?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The date is the 26th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And it was prepared by whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was signed by Lidija Pintar, who is a Croat and who issued a guarantee for this family so that they could come to Croatia. This is an important document for our line of questioning of the witness. We will touch upon also her family and explain how the exchanges functioned and how people could cross over to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, I hope this is just a language thing again, but I think that the counsel can of course ask the witness -- elicit anything from the witness that might throw light on this document and ask her questions about her exchange, but it's not counsel's role in cross-examination to explain how the exchanges function and how people cross to Croatia. That's -- counsel's not here giving evidence. So I hope he's not going to pursue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- a line like that if the witness cannot provide any information in this document. He's not going to continue to pursue a line that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- the witness cannot help him on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I had that in mind. That's why I asked how the witness was going to deal with this document. So when he explained I thought let's hear how the questions will be and how much the witness knows, if anything, about this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry again, Your Honour. Counsel have not provided us with an English translation. We just have the original they disclosed to us previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Krgovic has got spare copies for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document consists of two pages.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document consists of two pages. On the first page we have the statement and the text of the statement; on the second page we have the appostille seal, which was not been translated. And in connection with this document, I'd only be interested for the witness to read out the text on the seal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What seal?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stated that the second page of the B/C/S version of the appostille seal has not been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So that's the seal you wanted the witness to look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam, please look at that seal. Can you read the text on the round seal?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're thinking of the small seal? It's very small. "Republic of Croatia" on top, "municipality". I cannot see.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: That will be enough, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Krgovic. Apart from the seal on page 2, none of the rest has been translated either, because the only translation we have is -- well, the first page, with the list of the Cerninski family members and so on and so forth. Page 2, we don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second page was given also for translation. The first page of translation arrived. The second did not. If you want to, I can read it out, the second page, together with the witness. The second page is just a confirmation of the authorised body concerning this statement signed by the given person, and that taxes have been paid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But Mr. Krgovic, you can't give us the translation yourself, because you are counsel. What you should have done is to ask the Translation Unit why they didn't translate the second page. So it's not a complete document, as far as the official language is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The substance of this document, the first page - and I'll just ask for an ID number of this document at this time - and we will ask the witness to read out the second page, if you deem it necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, it's not up to the Trial Chamber to deem it necessary. It's your case. It's you who -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For me, it was enough that the witness read out that what she did read out on the seal, appostille seal. That is enough for my questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, are you aware of the fact that the Exchange Commission of the HVO, which was on the other side, didn't wish to accept persons who wished to go to Croatia without a previous statement or written invitation of somebody from Croatia itself?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you thinking of the HVO in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You were in Dragalici, you had the HVO commission waiting for you, and it was a commission from Orasje, and their president of -- their Exchange Commission?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And from there, that you left for Domaljevac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Are you aware that persons who wished to go to Croatia joined their families, or to go and live there, that they had to have a guarantee of their relatives, their friends from Croatia in order to be able to go to Croatia after the exchange took place?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the first time that I hear of such a possibility, even though I know that my sister from Switzerland was looking for me via the International Red Cross. She wasn't the only one. Others also. And in view of the fact that I was being requested from different sides, that was the reason that I had difficulties in being exchanged.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you know that Croatia didn't want to receive any refugees without a written guarantee of a person who will cover the costs of their stay and lodging in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to rectify. I am a citizen of Croatia and I am from -- also have the citizenship of Bosnia, so I was returning from one of my countries to the other country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel, the question has not been answered. The witness has explained her own situation, so I was wondering whether you still wanted your question answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, I would like to know the following: Do you know that if somebody wanted to go into Croatia after the exchange, that person needed a guarantee, and that Croatia refused to accept a person of any ethnicity without a special guarantee issued by a resident of Croatia stating that this resident of Croatia would cover the costs of the other person's staying in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I had money in Croatia, and I still have it now. Nobody had to cover my costs. I was simply returning home.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: I simply asked you whether you knew about this fact. Maybe it did not apply to you because you were a citizen of Croatia. But do you know that the people who wanted to go to Croatia after the exchange had to have a guarantee?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were few cases similar to mine. Nobody informed me of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, no, no, no. Just answer the question as put to you by counsel: Did you know about that, that there was a requirement of a guarantee? Just answer it yes or no. Did you know? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Your Honours, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And as far as your boyfriend is concerned, do you know that he needed a guarantee to come and rejoin you in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my boyfriend is concerned, I didn't know anything. I didn't even know whether he was alive.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did he follow you to Croatia? Did he come with you to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four days after the exchange.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And did somebody have to issue a guarantee for him to be able to stay in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My family gave a guarantee for him, and immediately thereafter we got married.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So, madam, you did know that if somebody wanted to go and stay in Croatia from Bosnia and Herzegovina, that that person needed a guarantee?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about it then.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, let me ask you about the Cerninski family. You knew Stipe Cerninski, who was the director of the post office?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My husband worked in the post office.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And Angela was exchanged with you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember whether she was.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: She was the mother of Stipe Crninski?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember whether I saw the lady in question in that commotion.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, can you please take a look at the date of this guarantee. It's highlighted in yellow.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: It says 26th of August, 1992 as the date the guarantee was issued.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So that means that the guarantee was issued on that day, 26th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, Your Honours, I would like to have this document admitted, but as an ID document for the time being, until we finalise the translation of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will have it marked for identification until the translation is completed, and also, this witness hasn't said anything that would warrant the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have a number of these documents which explain this. I simply wanted to cover this document with this witness, simply because members of the Cerninski family were exchanged together with this witness. And we will refer back to this again in the proceedings, and right now all I wanted to see is whether this witness knows about the facts regarding the guarantee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We shall have it marked for identification only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I don't need any more.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be D66/3 ter ID and D66/3 ID, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, you took these words implying that you wouldn't be exchanged so easily very seriously, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: On page 19 of yesterday's transcript, when asked by the Prosecutor about how you were taken to Zasavica, you said that you had expected to be exchanged and that when you were taken to Zasavica, you had already had two bags prepared to be taken with you to exchange.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And you did not unpack these bags, apparently, until the 7th of September, when you were taken to Zasavica.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So you were hoping, you had a great desire to leave Samac, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Quite logically, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, when you answered Prosecutor's questions yesterday, on page 21, you said that at the checkpoint in Zasavica you saw members of the special police for the first time. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That special police, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: When you had an interview with the OTP in May, you stated that you were taken to be examined by Dr. Nogic under the police escort. Do you know any of those policemen that escorted you? I'm here referring to the policemen who escorted you to Dr. Nogic. Were they the same policemen whom you had previously identified as members of the special police?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of them was assigned to escort, and I didn't know the others.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Well, I didn't quite understand you. So were they the same policemen as those whom you had previously seen at the Zasavica checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was a duty policeman at the Zasavica checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And you identified them as members of the special police?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is how they introduced themselves to me.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And Simo Krunic went with you, if I understood you properly.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And every time you went to get a shot, you were accompanied by armed guards. That's what you stated. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, but they were not always the same guards.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Were you able to move freely about Samac after receiving your shot?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On few occasions, accompanied by police, yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did you state to the Prosecutor that you went to Samac to buy cigarettes at Ilija Popovic's?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Can I just -- I just want to correct the record. Mrs. Kapetanovic never said that she went to Bosanski Samac to buy cigarettes. She said that on one occasion after she had been for her shot she took advantage of the opportunity to get some cigarettes. So I don't want the counsel putting on the record and implying that the purpose of her visit to the Bosanski Samac town was simply to purchase cigarettes and that she was permitted to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that it was during the same time that she went for the medication, for the injections?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, counsel said that: "Did you state to the Prosecutor you went to Samac to buy cigarettes?" And that's not what she said to the Prosecutor. When she went, she went to Samac and she did say she went to buy cigarettes at Ilija Popovic's, but that was after she was in Samac for her shots and she took advantage of the opportunity to buy some cigarettes. The quotation there is incorrect from counsel and it implies that she was permitted to go to Samac for the purposes of cigarettes, which is not what she stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is how I read this, but I will read out the unofficial statement of this witness, which says as follows: "The owner of the bar where I normally bought cigarettes was Ignjo Popovic, and since he wasn't at the bar at the time, bar/restaurant, I went to look for him." Can you tell me, please, when was this? Because based on this material that I received from the Prosecution, it says here the owner of the bar where I normally bought cigarettes. So this was something that was customary; at least, this is how I read this. I didn't say that the witness only went into town to buy cigarettes, but it flowed after my question when I asked her about the shots and whether she was able to move freely about the town upon receiving her shot. It came after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like the witness to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's clear that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, you saw what this was all about. When you went to get your shots, did you stop by the bar of Ignjo Popovic to buy cigarettes there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, I went to buy cigarettes at the bar together with the police, so accompanied by the special police, and since I did not find the owner there, I was taken to the mosque to be shown what my brothers had done to the mosque. When I said that I normally bought cigarettes there, I have to say that I bought cigarettes at the time when it was very difficult to come by cigarettes in Samac, and it didn't have to do anything with the event that I described. It's a different period of time.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Well, did you find this person where you wanted to buy cigarettes?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did find him that day, or perhaps some of his associates or family members, and I think that I did manage to buy cigarettes that day. I'm not quite sure, but I know that I did come back with cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, I would like to ask you now about an event that you brought up, and it has to do with your neighbour, Vera Avdic. Do you know that Vera Avdic hails from Gornja Dubica in Odzak municipality?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that very well.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And that her parents live there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that very well too.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And they were exchanged and for a while lived in Vera's apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You know that the husband of Vera Abdic was killed in Grebnice as a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You mentioned having seen Vera Avdic unload the wood stove of a tractor some time in the summer of 1992, after Odzak was taken over by the Serb forces. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you know where personal belongings of her parents were?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them personally.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you know that this electric stove was brought by Vera Avdic from Dubica and that it belonged to her parents?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I have to correct you. It wasn't an electric stove; it was a wood stove.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. You said a wood stove. Do you know that those items, including the stove, in fact belonged to her parents?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vera Avdic personally told me where she got those items, so that there couldn't be any mistake regarding that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you know that the mother of Vera Avdic is a Croat?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And that she couldn't take her stove when she was exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I also know where Vera's brother was, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And you still stand by your previous claim that these were not personal belongings or property of Vera Avdic, but rather, that she had received it as a reward for her husband's being a member of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't the only stove that Vera Avdic had delivered to our building.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did she really personally tell you that she had received that stove from the 4th Detachment? Did she clearly, specifically state that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically that she had received it from the 4th Detachment, but that she -- that was a reward for her husband's participation in the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Her husband was killed?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, and I regret that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, I would like to open up a new topic now pertaining to the ICRC's visit to Zasavica. You told us yesterday that the ICRC came to Zasavica and that you were present when some explanation took place regarding the treatment of people who resided in Zasavica. You also mentioned a lady interpreter who was at the meeting. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did you know that lady interpreter from before?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So she was not from Samac, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, she wasn't.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You said yesterday that she spoke with a Serbian dialect. I didn't quite gather whether she spoke Ekavian dialect, or how did you conclude that she spoke a Serbian dialect?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all residents of Samac have a very specific dialect, and she spoke a little bit different, so it sounded like Ekavian dialect.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Did she leave together with the representatives of the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the one who left, sir. She remained there.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: But after that, when the representatives of ICRC left Zasavica, you did not see her again in Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you know that the ICRC had its own interpretation service and took its own interpreters to all negotiations and meetings?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And was this interpreter able to hear everything you said to Simo Krunic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She sat nearby. She was able to hear.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, do you know that the ICRC has a rule that when conducting an interview with the persons affected, no representative of local authorities can be present?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in what capacity Mr. Krunic was there then.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: We spent quite a lot of time dealing with this meeting, and as far as I gathered, you did not address yourself directly to the ICRC but rather to Mr. Krunic.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was directed towards him.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: But you addressed yourself to Mr. Krunic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because he remained there later on as well, whereas the others stayed there only for a short period of time.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, I would like to ask you several questions regarding your attempt to get exchanged on the 7th of October. You brought this up yesterday when examined by the Prosecution. You said that on the previous day you were told that you were on the list of people to be exchanged on the 7th of October, 1992. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Do you remember somebody else who was supposed to be exchanged with you from Zasavica as well on that same day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I regret to say that I cannot remember that person right now, but I know that I didn't go alone.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So you cannot remember the name of any person who, together with you, on that day, was transported from Zasavica to Bosanski Samac, to the area in front of the secondary school, which is where the people left from to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not think -- I have not thought about that in the past ten years, and I can't tell you that right now. Such things were not important to me.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, you mentioned yesterday that there were several groups of people standing in front of the buses. There was a group of you, people from Zasavica, then there was a group of beaten-up people, and then there were also people from Bosanski Samac. So can you remember the name of anybody else who was present there on the 7th of October, when you failed to get exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, very well.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Can you tell me who went then, on that day?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The wife of Dedo Halilovic, with her son. I can't remember his name right now. I think it was Faruk or something like that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And you can't remember anybody from Zasavica?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must have been the people whom I didn't know very well. I was very ill at the time and very much scared, on account of all of that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Can you tell me, please: What is the name of Dedo Halilovic's wife? Was it Ismeta?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Ismeta.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And there was a child with her?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a son, some 15 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to introduce as a document a list of people to be exchanged, dated 5th November, 1992. I apologise. These are the women designated to be exchanged on the 7th of October. This is the Prosecution's document. We don't have the translation. Because this witness mentioned this event, and this is the Prosecution's document, and only upon hearing the testimony of this witness we'll learn that she attempted to get exchanged on the 7th of October. So if we could please have this document introduced as an ID document. It has only a heading and a list of names. Immediately upon receiving this information, we sent this document to be translated, and, as I told you, we learned of this upon hearing this witness's testimony that she had attempted to get exchanged on the 7th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: May I just correct the record on that? Because it's simply not true. The fact that this witness was taken for an exchange earlier in October and that she ended up in fact not being put on the exchange has been part of her statement which was disclosed -- it's paragraph 91 of her statement. It was disclosed to Defence before this witness took the stand. They've had it for the whole time that the prior witness has been on the stand. That was three weeks. So it's simply not yesterday that they heard it. It is a Prosecution document to the extent that in the process of disclosure under Rule 66(A), we disclosed it, but this is not the first time that they know this witness went through to one failed exchange and wasn't exchanged. So just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's important to clarify that so that we know. Mr. Krgovic, it's now Mr. Lukic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. Let us just clarify this. We don't want to create an even greater confusion. We hope the Trial Chamber will understand the position of the Defence of Miroslav Tadic, for a technical reason. The Prosecution delivered to us the lists for exchange as their evidence. These were all in B/C/S, and we did receive it during the discovery stage. We also have our lists that we disclosed to the Prosecution. We always try to prepare the translation in advance so that we can have it for each relevant witness, but sometimes we can't coordinate this perfectly, and sometimes errors do occur. So this list and the other list, dated 5th November, were submitted for translation. We have not received the translation yet, but we hereby apply to you to allow us to introduce this document as an ID document, and we hope to receive translation in a few days. And I do apologise to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Krgovic, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you put on the ELMO this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have it numbered for identification purposes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D67/3 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, please take a good look at this list.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Please read the heading, the one that is highlighted in yellow, and not fast, please.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republika Srpska, Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, commission for exchange of prisoners and arrested civilians, Bosanski Samac, the 5th of October, 1992. List of women to be exchanged in Dragalici on the 7th of October, 1992."

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at these names. Do you know anybody else in addition to the wife of Dedo Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm glad here to see the name of Ismeta Halilovic, which means that I recalled correctly. And it means that I was with her in front of that school in Samac. It was -- this concerns this lady who was not arrested.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, this -- your name is not on this list; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regrettably not. And according to what it says, the list was drawn up on the 5th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this list, and I see that by hand, a name was added, a name of a lady, and I'm surprised that mine wasn't added also.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, may I ask you: Was there anybody else, except you, that had been excluded from this exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, I didn't notice anything similar concerning others as to what happened to me.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: A person by the name of Cakara, his nickname, Cakara, Naser, he didn't allow you to board the bus; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was standing in front of the bus with a list of people, and he allowed people to board only if their names were on his list.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: This person, Cakara, was a policeman before the war?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Kapetanovic. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, could we just get the witness to translate the notation next to the number 14, Anica Jelavic. It might be difficult to re-examine if we don't know what the handwritten notation says at all. So if we could just find out what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you repeat that where? MR. DI FAZIO: Number 14, handwritten notation, number 14, Jelavic, Anica and there's some sort of handwritten notation with a date next to it and it may have significance, it may not, I don't know. But until it's translated, we can't decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam Kapetanovic, can you read it out for us? That's what's written by hand.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Exchanged on the 29th of January, 1993," or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: It means that on that day she wasn't exchanged. She was exchanged on the 29th of January, 1993. How do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't personally know this woman, and I don't know when this was entered by hand. I don't know what happened to this woman.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: If it stands that she was exchanged on the 29th of January, 1993, it means that on this day on the paper she didn't -- she wasn't exchanged.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it would mean that if this is true, this is one person less and that I could have been her replacement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but that whole evidence is really guesswork, because the witness has already said she didn't know this lady, she didn't know what happened to her. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I've finished with that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Kapetanovic, a few more questions concerning your exchange. You were exchanged on the 5th of November, 1992, in a place called Dragalici?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: That took place at the gas station? If you recall.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And that area was under the UN protection?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And that place -- in that place the UN representatives asked you if you wanted to cross over?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: On that occasion, when the UN representative asked that question, did anybody threaten you or pressure you or coerce you either to stay or to go?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, during that moment, there was no pressure.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And if you didn't cross over, you could have returned to Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, into the camp of Samac.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: But you decided to accept the exchange and join your family and your then boyfriend. That's what you stated.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted my freedom.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You went -- were taken to that petrol pump, which was rather far out from Samac. It was a safe area. There was no military operations there.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived there, there was no shooting, and it was quiet.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And all around you were the UN representatives. I suppose you saw them.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Also when you entered and you left the zone?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Samac was under the Serb control and was shelled; you mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Grebnice, Domaljevac, where you went after your exchange, was also shelled in the operation, in this zone?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were honoured with such shelling and arms fire that for continue days it was echoing.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: After that you went to Grebnice?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Madam, the place where the UN representative asked you whether you want to cross over or return to Samac, did anybody return from that line back to Samac and who was on the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of such a person. The person didn't do it on that day, but in the course of the preceding exchange. That was Mr. Marko Filipovic. Was brought to the exchange line. He stated that he doesn't want to go into the exchange, and he was returned from Zasavica to Samac. And let me add that the lady is a Serb, of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So you know only of this single case?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only of this single case.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You described that in the exchange also your dog Pegi was involved. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember. She was always with me.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You said the dog was exchanged for a child. You explained it yesterday that it was in addition to your name, there was a plus 1, as if it was a child.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told I would be exchanged, and it was understood that my dog would go too, and I remember that it was discussed that the exchange would be for a child.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: You also mentioned this "plus 1" next to your name as if a child was involved.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly I said it. Otherwise, let me say that I treat my dog as my child.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, Your Honours, I would like to enter into evidence the list of exchange dated the 5th of November, 1992. This document, as well as the previous ones, hasn't been translated, for the reasons explained by my colleague Lukic, and I'd only ask for the ID number. We won't dwell on it long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I want to find out, Mr. Krgovic, the reason you want this list shown, is it to show whether the addition of "plus 1" regarding the witness's dog is on the list? Is that the only reason you want it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are some marks on this exchange list which explains also child, or the status of the person, and her name is on the list.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, have you seen this list?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I've seen it only now.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Could you read the heading, please, underlined in yellow.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republic of Srpska, municipality of Serbian Samac, commission for the exchange of prisoners and arrested civilians. Samac, the 5th of November, 1992, a list of persons, civilians, who went, on the 5th of November, 1992, to Croatia."

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Mrs. Kapetanovic, please look at page 2, number 45 and 46. Could you read out these names?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 45, Cerninski, Ferdo, born 1913, and number 46, Crninski, Angela, born in 1925.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Are these the same people we're talking about, for whom we've seen that statement of guarantee?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And these guarantees were issued on the 26th of August, 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, according to your document.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And they were answered -- they were exchanged together with you?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it says on the document: Persons, civilians, who left on the 5th of November, 1992, to Croatia. I am surprised that you stated there that we are all going to Croatia, because we were exchanged within Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: It wasn't us, madam. Please, madam, read out the number 31.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stanisic Jelena, born 1957.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: Is this your name?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: And this plus next to the name, what does it mean? Do they represent the number of children?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no crosses and no children. I'm reading the names of persons, civilians, who left. So my dog wasn't a person, civilian.

utterances.speaker: THE PROSECUTOR YESTERDAY
utterances.text: So he wasn't exchanged as a person, civilian. And on the third page, number 88, what does -- please read the name and then what is stated in the brackets.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the bracket, it says "pregnant."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher. I've finished with this document. I have no further questions. I've finished my cross-examination. [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Kapetanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have an ID number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D68/3 ter ID. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, Your Honours, my co-counsel, Mr. Novic, will conduct this cross-examination today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, what we -- the information the Trial Chamber has is that he's a legal assistant. He has not been appointed to replace co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He is in fact acting as a co-counsel during the temporary period when my co-counsel is absent, and he's a practicing lawyer and professor of criminal law, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but there is no document from the Registrar to replace him as co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, that is arrangement made with the Registrar for this limited period. Yes, the question is yes, there is no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. The document the Trial Chamber has seen is that he's a legal assistant. He's part of your team, of the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But due to this outstanding situation with my co-counsel, Mr. Vukovic, I make an arrangement with the Registrar that for this limited period of couple of weeks, Mr. Novic, who is practicing lawyer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. That's not the dispute. The point is there is no document replacing Mr. Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, not officially. It's just an arrangement with the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That doesn't mean he has the right of audience before the Trial Chamber. He doesn't have the right of audience.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So the cross-examination should be done by yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No problem at all, but I'm just asking for this particular -- I was not informed prior to that. My understanding was that when the arrangement was made with the Registrar, that everything is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think a step further should have been taken, because he can sit in court, but as to whether or not he has audience, there has to be a document formally appointing him to replace the co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I will do that immediately this afternoon and we shall obtain this paper for the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. If you verify that with the Registrar, that will be fine with the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Madam Kapetanovic. I'm the Defence counsel for Blagoje Simic. Could you tell me, because you stated on a number of occasions, including to the Prosecution and in front of this Court, in your statement also of 1998, that you have four brothers.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have four brothers and three sisters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Among these brothers and sisters, you said -- stated that four brothers and a sister were members of the 108th Slavonia Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: 108th Slavonia Brigade is a part of the armed formations of the Croatian army; isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you have any information when these three brothers and the sister became members of the 108th Slavonia Brigade of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the precise data.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But you do have contacts with your brothers and sisters?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do contact them, but I never asked for the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As it's an undisputed fact that they were members of this brigade in April 1992, can we determine this as an undisputed fact?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I believe that they were members of the 108th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And what posts did they occupy, your four brothers, if you can enumerate it for us?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My oldest brother was in a unit with the medical doctors. He was a driver of an ambulance. My sister, as she had a radio transmitter, she worked in their staff headquarters and working in the area of logistics. Another brother only arrived from the army, and he joined the infantry. I don't know what kind. And two of them were attached to the command and connected with the civilian activities, precisely, their refugee --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So they were all in the 108th Slavonia Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This 108th Slavonia Brigade was attached to my town, Slavonski Samac. They belonged to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Slavonski Samac is 50 metres from Bosanski Samac. It's divided by a river and it's in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that one of your brothers just came from the army and he joined this other army. Maybe I didn't understand you properly.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had the misfortune of serving in the air force in Serbia. I don't recall the town where they worked in the subterranean part of the airport. And instead of abandoning the army after his period of service, he was retained as a Croat another two months. And I'm surprised they let him go alive from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you properly that he left the JNA in March 1992, and after that he joined the 108th Slavonia Brigade? Now, is that -- do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't in March 1992. You have to know that the war in Croatia was in 1991, and here we're dealing of persons with a Croatian citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, correct me: When did he leave the JNA and join the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but he left the JNA prior to the breakout of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I don't know exactly how much earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Probably in the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly somewhere there, but I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your sister, that's an undisputed fact that she is a radio communications specialist?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was dealing in this only as an amateur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, why do we want all these details? Isn't it sufficient that her brothers and sisters were in this Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So why do we want the details in relation to the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's important, Your Honour. Now we are going to the closing link.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She worked with the professional equipment, radio equipment. You stated that to the Prosecution and here.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She worked with radio equipment for amateurs. What is really professional equipment, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This activity was in the area of social protection and All Peoples Defence?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This radio station was transferred from that organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Before the station was transferred in 1990 in Bosnia and Herzegovina, her activity was within the framework of all general defence and social protection?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The station was moved before the outbreak of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam Kapetanovic, please listen to me. Before 1990, do you have personal knowledge that radio amateurs were within the framework of All Peoples Defence and general protection of Bosnia and Herzegovina? And I'm speaking of prior to 1990.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know for Bosnia, but my sister lived in Croatia, and I don't know what the enforced laws were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will confirm the fact for me that your sister and your brothers had maintained contact with you while you were in Bosanski Samac, they in Slavonski Samac, from January 1992 up to your exchange?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must correct the date. From January 1992 until the beginning of the war, the 17th, the 16th of April, 1992. In that period, I had contacts with my family. After that, there was this lack of communication from that day to the 5th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the police of Bosanski Samac, there is information that your brothers, your sister, and you were, in fact, Croatian agent, intelligence agents, working for the Croatian army. Can you confirm that you were an intelligence agent in Bosanski Samac? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I'm hearing something of this sort. I have never been a Croatian agent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take our break and continue our proceedings at 12.50 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You're continuing with cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I understand the video director is not yet in, so we'll have no transmission. We'll just have to wait for a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In that case, Your Honour, I can maybe ask to go into closed session, because we don't need transmission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, but is the evidence supposed to be in closed session? I'm sure it's just a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I can use this break to take the opportunity and inform the Trial Chamber that in the meantime, I received the official translation of the document D67/3 ter, and also D68/3 ter, which is the list for exchange dated 5th November. I received this during the break, and I thought that perhaps after Mr. Pantelic finishes his cross-examination, we could introduce these documents in case, during the re-direct, there should be any questions regarding this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I want to find out from the Prosecution whether there's any objection. This is D68 and D67.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Can we have confirmation that they will retain the same numbers as exhibits?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. They will be tendered into evidence as exhibits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And can we get the English copies? Oh, the usher is not yet here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The director is in. You can proceed, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Yes. I -- okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Kapetanovic, in May 2002, you gave a statement to the Prosecution. I will give you a copy of that statement so that you can follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... give this statement to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is in your language. Please turn to page 7. I will read it out, and then if you can confirm whether I'm reading it out correctly. Page 7, paragraph 17. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Towards the end, your sentence goes as follows: "Before the before, my sister had professional radio equipment - she was involved as an amateur in ham radio links and she had a huge antenna. One could see that antenna from the distance of 5 kilometres from Bosanski Samac. The war was going on in Croatia, so she took the radio for the use of her unit, so that she had a radio. I unfortunately had a smaller radio that I used with the children of Salko Porobic. It was not of a large range." So this is what you stated to the Prosecutor sometime in May of this year; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, can you please tell me what this abbreviation, ham, h-a-m, stands for? You used it, so can you please explain it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go down this path, let me clarify this. This statement was taken by me from this witness when originally we were hoping that she may give part of her evidence under Rule 92 bis. In the interview with her, the interpreter with me was trying to explain that the sort of activities that her sister did with the radio was not on a professional basis. It was as an amateur. There's a saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Why don't we hear that from witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: This kind of explanation, we have a witness here. This is a criminal proceedings, Your Honour. We have our sources, why --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Because Mr. Pantelic is deliberately trying to put a gloss on the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you wait, Mr. Pantelic. Let's hear Ms. Reidy. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: So I said some sort of like radio ham, meaning that would be an English expression, expression I would use in English, and so the witness said "yes," or the translator said to me "Yes, that sort of thing." So I wrote down ham in inverted commas. It is not an abbreviation for anything. It's not a -- and obviously in the translation they just use the same thing, ham, translating it back into the language for the accused. So for Mr. Pantelic to try to go down the do you -- go down the road of suggesting that this witness used an abbreviation or a word that tried to reflect a unit is not true and I think it's a waste of this Court's time to do that. Because that's simply where the word "ham" came from and it is in inverted commas as a -- you know, ham meaning a slang word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. All right. Yes, Mr. Pantelic, you can go ahead --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: . I absolutely, I agree. Then this witness can say "I don't know anything about ham." Why are we listening all this stuff, you know? It's not fair. This witness is entitled to say "I don't know anything about abbreviation ham."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I should ask this question: What is the point of you're asking what type of radio --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It is not the point of, Your Honour, what type of radio is. I tried to clarify certain issues, from my point of view, which was said by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And this witness can say, "I didn't use abbreviation ham. That was used by the Prosecutor." And then we go on. It's very simple. Why do we have to hear all these submissions from my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. The Prosecution has to explain so that they give a clear picture as to how the interview was conducted, and that is important. So you can proceed, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please tell me, Mrs. Kapetanovic: When you said here, "Unfortunately I had a small radio," why was it unfortunately so? Did you regret the fact that it was a small one? Did you want to -- did you wish to have a larger one?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked a very good question, Mr. Pantelic. In view of the fact that there was such great pressure exerted and that they were looking for a large radio transmitter, I sincerely regretted the fact that I did not have one, because I would have handed it over right away and then I would spare myself the ensuing threats and pistols shoved in my head, and that is why I said that I regretted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what is the square area of your apartment?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 69.75 square metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How many rooms? Can you describe the apartment, please?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two rooms, kitchen, hallway, bathroom, balcony, dining-room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I asked you about how many rooms.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You lived with your then boyfriend, current husband; right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Why do you and your husband need a walkie-talkie to communicate between each other if you only have two rooms?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not procure these walkie-talkies with my current husband. It was purchased by my late husband, Stanisic, who was a great admirer of all things technical. My late husband was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's all very well, but I'm now going back to the reply you gave to this Trial Chamber in answer to a question put by the Prosecutor. You said that you had used walkie-talkie to communicate with your husband. Please don't wiggle. I'm asking you very directly: Why would you need a walkie-talkie in a two-room apartment to communicate with your husband? Please answer the question. Was that used perhaps for intelligence activities with your partners in Slavonski Samac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, that's all correct. It is true that I used that walkie-talkie with my husband, but while we were fishing. I was on the one bank and he was on the other bank, fishing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So that walkie-talkie wasn't simply intended for home use, in two rooms, in an apartment of 65 square metres; it was also used in the field?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was used on a pond, which is smaller than this room.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 32 of this document, paragraph 100. Paragraph 100, the first sentence: "I talked to the people from the other side, and I gave them all the information I had ..." As I take it, this was after your exchange and that you gave information to the other side. Won't you agree with me that this information was furnished by you to the Croatian army and its intelligence service and it had to do with the events in Bosanski Samac during your stay there?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You used a wrong term. It was not Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, to whom from the other side did you give information that you had?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, my statement reflects that I was taken to Bosnia, which means that that was the HVO, not HV.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you gave a statement to the representatives of the HVO and their Security Services; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave it to the people who were responsible for civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It was the security services of the HVO, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the people who were with the HVO and were in charge of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you, for the third time: Were they members of the HVO security service? Do you have any information to that effect or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Pantelic said it himself. He's asked for the third time. The witness has answered the question, who these people were. They were people responsible for the civilians, they were people responsible for the civilians. And I think for Mr. Pantelic to keep asking the question amounts to badgering. I let it go twice, but this is the third time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: She is avoiding the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. She has given the answer according to her knowledge. If you don't agree with her answer, that doesn't mean that she is avoiding the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When was the last time, Mrs. Kapetanovic, that you talked to Dragan Lukac? Did you hear my question, madam?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, when was the last time you talked to Dragan Lukac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was some kind of a celebration in 1993 at his father's. I had an opportunity to greet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And you had no contact in recent months?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw this man again in my life. This was the last time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: But he uses the same term as you do, "Samac town camp." Did you -- have you read his book perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I'm surprised that it's only the two of us who used that term, "Samac town camp." I read many books.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Have you read the books by Dragan -- or a book by Dragan Lukac?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certain segments of it, yes, but it's difficult for me to go back to wartime events, and I try to avoid it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Please turn to page 14 of the document in front of you, paragraph 39. In that paragraph, you mention organising -- for some women to go to their villages, Tisina, Hasici, and so on. And then you go on to say as follows: "These women brought back to us the information on what was taking place outside." Did you state this to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and I can confirm that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that these women were from two villages, Tisina and Hasici, who were on the front line, can you tell us whether these women also belonged to your intelligence group in Samac, since they furnished the information back to you? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: The counsel is putting to the witness that she had an intelligence group in Samac, and whatever theory he wants to put up on his defence case is something, but that's simply not true and it's inappropriate to put that in the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: She can simply say no, Your Honour. I have certain allegations, certain informations with regard to this radio transmissions. So why we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. It's the way you put the question to her. You can make the assertion to her and then she can deny it; thereafter you add whatever questions you want to add, instead of putting them in one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I just tried to make a puzzle, because I have various informations here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, Mrs. Kapetanovic, tell me, please: These women who went out and brought back the information on what was taking place, did they have some kind of an intelligence link with you so that you could relate this information later on to Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I had no opportunity to relate any information to anybody else. Can you tell me by what means I could have done that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, by using walkie-talkie. Isn't that what you used to convey information?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, we are referring to it as a walkie-talkie. I am sorry that I don't have it in front of me now so that I could ask you who could you send any kind of information by means of that walkie-talkie.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, you explained that to the Prosecution on page 8932, on the 5th of June, when asked by the Prosecution to explain what was this walkie-talkie all about, this Motorola. You replied the following, on lines 13 and 15: [In English] "What I mean by this is the complete equipment, including the radio, with its frequencies, and the walkie-talkie, that was used for communicating. That is a radio transmitter, this whole equipment." [Interpretation] Do you remember stating this in front of this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. Just please tell me: Do you remember saying this to this Trial Chamber? Let's not go into details.

utterances.speaker: JELENA KAPETANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are now discussing my sister's equipment, not my equipment. You are now referring to Croatia, not to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
